pluss::note::full_like¶

Back to Note Factory API Reference

Signatures¶

Note pluss::note::full_like(const Note& like, string_view value)

Borrow Another Note’s Shape, Choose A New Value¶

full_like() reads the shape of an existing Note and returns a fresh Note of that same shape with value in every cell. It is full with the sizes list replaced by “whatever shape like has”.

Use it whenever you already hold a Note whose geometry you want to match — a mask the same size as a text column, a placeholder grid congruent with a parsed table, a reset buffer shaped like the input. Taking the shape from like keeps the two in lock-step even if the source shape changes, and avoids restating extents that are only correct by coincidence.

Only the shape is copied. The contents of like are ignored; its encoding is ignored too — full_like always produces a UTF-8-mode Note. For a bytes-mode result with a borrowed shape, use full_bytes_like.

like must be a defined Note (any that the factory functions return qualifies). The result is a new, independent Note; later edits to it do not touch like, and vice versa.

Example 1: A Placeholder Grid Congruent With Another Note¶

const auto grid = pluss::note::make({{"a", "b", "c"}, {"d", "e", "f"}});
std::cout << pluss::note::print(pluss::note::full_like(grid, "?")) << "\n";

Output¶

Note(shape=[2, 3], dim=2, numel=6, encoding=utf8)
[
  ["?", "?", "?"], 
  ["?", "?", "?"]
]

Shape [2, 3] came from grid; every cell is the new value "?", and grid itself is untouched.

See Also¶

  • pluss::note::full: supply the shape as an explicit sizes list instead.

  • pluss::note::empty_like: full_like(like, "").

  • pluss::note::full_bytes_like: the bytes-mode counterpart.
